content.text: I fixed the three failing sheets by changing only the authoritative figure briefs — the specification text, claims and numeral table are untouched, since none of the failures were text defects.

input.summary: Three drawing sheets failed the gate; all three are repaired in the Markdown figure briefs only, so the pipeline re-renders and re-inspects fresh pixels. FIG. 1: numeral 100 was anchored 25 units from the sheet boundary because the dashed installation rectangle sat at the periphery — the brief now requires a wide inset for that rectangle and specifies an endpoint on the upper side in the clear band above the branch conductor, deep inside the sheet. FIG. 2: the run below the contactor rendered leftwards and the control-pilot-to-vehicle-connector link was missing, leaving a dead-end stub, so the brief is rebuilt with unambiguous direction language (turn towards the right side of the drawing area, away from the left edge), explicit named endpoints for every line, and an explicit statement that neither end of the joining line is free and that no other line leaves the bottom of the vehicle connector block. FIG. 4: numeral 216 landed on a rectangle boundary and reviewers split on which rectangle it identified — the brief now requires shape-identifying leaders to stop at the interior centre rather than on an edge or vertex, identifies 216 as the lowest shape below diamond 214 and 212 as the rectangle between the two diamonds, and calls for wider spacing so consecutive shapes are plainly separated. No claim, description, numeral-table or embodiment change was needed, and none was made; nothing in the drawings was treated as authority for the invention. Note, as in the original brief: no prior-art search was run, so the art considered may be incomplete.
changes: FIG-1.md: dashed charging-installation rectangle must be inset well inside the drawing area (at least one tenth of the sheet width of blank margin on every side), so its line work is not near the sheet boundary.

FIG-1.md: numeral 100 leader endpoint respecified to the upper side of the dashed rectangle in its right portion, with the numeral in the clear band between that side and the branch conductor, and an explicit minimum distance from every sheet edge.

FIG-2.md rebuilt: the run below the contactor is now stated to turn towards the right side of the drawing area, away from the left edge, and to end on the left side of the vehicle connector block, with both of its ends named so it cannot render leftwards or dead-end.

FIG-2.md rebuilt: the connection between the control-pilot interface block and the vehicle connector block is now a single explicitly routed line ending on the lower edge of the vehicle connector block, with a statement that neither end is free and that no other line extends downward from that block.

FIG-2.md rebuilt: the sensor-to-controller line, the isolated local bus and its two branches now have named terminations and explicit non-crossing relations to the incoming supply line, the horizontal run and the joining line.
FIG-4.md: added a rule that a leader identifying one of the column shapes ends at the centre of that shape's interior and never on an edge or vertex.

FIG-4.md: numeral 216 respecified as the lowest shape in the column, below diamond 214, with the endpoint at the rectangle's centre and clear of all four edges; numeral 212 respecified as the rectangle between diamond 210 and diamond 214 to remove the ambiguity the reviewers split on.
FIG-4.md: shapes to be drawn large enough and spaced far enough apart that consecutive shapes are plainly separated, with a clear blank margin below the lowest shape.

patches.find: A dashed rectangle encloses the whole diagram and represents the charging installation, shown schematically.
patches.replace: A dashed rectangle encloses the whole diagram and represents the charging installation, shown schematically. This dashed rectangle is inset well inside the drawing area: a blank margin of at least one tenth of the sheet width separates each of its four sides from the nearest edge of the sheet, and no part of it approaches the filing margins.
patches.why: Numeral 100 is anchored on this rectangle; the sheet failed because that endpoint fell 25 units from the sheet boundary. Insetting the depicted target moves the anchor deep inside the drawing area.

patches.find: - 100 charging installation: leader ends on the dashed enclosing rectangle.
patches.replace: - 100 charging installation: leader ends on the upper side of the dashed enclosing rectangle, in the right portion of that side, above the rightmost block of the row. The endpoint lies deep inside the sheet, no closer to any edge of the sheet than one tenth of the sheet width. The numeral sits below the endpoint, inside the dashed rectangle in the clear band between its upper side and the horizontal line, and the short leader rises from the numeral to that upper side, crossing no line work.
patches.why: Gives the leader a grounded interior anchor with an explicit minimum clearance from the sheet boundary, curing the ungrounded-anchor failure.

patches.find: The staged reduction step (210) and the welded-contactor isolation step (214) are diamonds. Every shape other than the two diamonds is a rectangle.
patches.replace: The staged reduction step (210) and the welded-contactor isolation step (214) are diamonds. Every shape other than the two diamonds is a rectangle. The eight shapes are drawn large enough, and the vertical gap between each shape and the next is wide enough, that consecutive shapes are plainly separated from one another. The column as a whole stays well inside the drawing area, with a clear blank margin between the lowest shape and the lower edge of the sheet.
patches.why: Crowded, similarly sized shapes let the 216 endpoint be read as belonging to a neighbouring rectangle; clear separation makes the intended target unambiguous.

patches.find: The part names listed below are semantic identifiers only and do not appear as drawing text. Each reference numeral sits clear of the line work on a short straight leader that crosses no other leader and no line work.
patches.replace: The part names listed below are semantic identifiers only and do not appear as drawing text. Each reference numeral sits clear of the line work on a short straight leader that crosses no other leader and no line work. Where a numeral identifies one of the shapes in the column, its leader ends at the centre of the interior of that shape and does not stop on any edge, side or vertex of any shape.
patches.why: Numeral 216 was rejected because its endpoint sat on a rectangle boundary, which made the identified shape ambiguous to review.

patches.find: - 212 ordered shedding step: leader ends well inside the rectangle immediately below the upper diamond (210).
patches.replace: - 212 ordered shedding step: leader ends at the centre of the interior of the rectangle that lies immediately below the upper diamond (210) and immediately above the lower diamond (214), that is, the sixth shape from the top of the column, clear of all four of its edges.
patches.why: The rejected 216 leader was read as pointing at this rectangle; naming each rectangle by its position between the diamonds separates the two targets.

patches.find: - 216 conditional reclosure step: leader ends well inside the bottom rectangle.
patches.replace: - 216 conditional reclosure step: leader ends at the centre of the interior of the bottom rectangle, which is the lowest shape of the column, the eighth shape from the top, and lies below the lower diamond (214). The endpoint is clear of all four edges of that rectangle by at least a quarter of the rectangle's height, and it is not on the rectangle between the two diamonds. The numeral sits outside the column to the left of that bottom rectangle, and its short leader enters through the left edge and stops at the centre.
patches.why: Fixes the misplaced numeral 216 by fixing the endpoint in the interior of the correct, positionally identified rectangle.

rewrites.why: The sheet failed on three connected geometry defects: the run below the contactor rendered leftwards into a foreign line, the control-pilot to vehicle-connector connection was absent, and what was drawn instead formed a dead end. Each line therefore needs both of its ends named and its direction stated without reliance on the word 'right' alone, so the routing has to be rebuilt rather than spot-edited.
rewrites.text:
# FIG. 2

A flat schematic diagram of one connector channel in plain black line work on white, no shading and no words in the drawing area other than the reference numerals listed below. All line work stays well inside the drawing area, clear of the filing margins.

A dashed rectangle occupies the left and central portion of the drawing area and represents the first connector channel.

A solid vertical line enters from above, crosses the top side of the dashed rectangle at a point in the left portion of that top side, and continues downward inside the rectangle, as the incoming branch supply. A contactor interrupts this line in the upper half of the dashed rectangle, shown schematically as a small empty square outline straddling the vertical line, the line meeting the outline above and below. This is the only square outline in the drawing area.

Below the contactor the vertical line continues downward to a corner point at about the middle height of the dashed rectangle. At that corner the line turns towards the right side of the drawing area, that is, away from the left edge of the sheet and towards the electric vehicle, and runs horizontally to the left side of an empty rectangular block that straddles the right side of the dashed rectangle and represents the vehicle connector, shown schematically. The two ends of this horizontal run are the corner below the contactor at its left end and the left side of the vehicle connector block at its right end, so the run has no free end and does not travel towards the left edge of the sheet.

A small empty circle outline straddles this horizontal run between the corner and the vehicle connector block and represents the connector current sensor, shown schematically. This is the only circle in the drawing area.

A solid line leaves the top of the circle outline and runs straight upward, crossing the top side of the dashed rectangle and stopping a short distance above it, representing the connection to the edge controller. It lies to the right of the incoming supply line and crosses no other line.

An empty rectangular block sits in the lower region of the dashed rectangle, below the horizontal run and below the corner, and represents the control-pilot interface.

One single solid line joins the control-pilot interface block to the vehicle connector block. It leaves the right side of the control-pilot interface block, runs horizontally towards the right side of the drawing area, then turns upward and rises to meet the lower edge of the vehicle connector block, where it stops. Its upward portion lies to the right of the left side of the vehicle connector block, so that it crosses neither the horizontal run from the contactor nor any other line. Neither end of this joining line is free: one end is on the control-pilot interface block and the other is on the lower edge of the vehicle connector block. No other line extends downward from the vehicle connector block.

Right of the dashed rectangle a larger rounded rectangle represents an electric vehicle, shown schematically. A short solid line joins the right side of the vehicle connector block to the left side of the rounded rectangle.

A solid horizontal line enters from the left edge of the drawing area and crosses the left side of the dashed rectangle in its lower region, as the isolated local bus. Inside the dashed rectangle it branches two ways. One branch continues towards the right side of the drawing area, passing below the corner and below the horizontal run, and ends on the left side of the control-pilot interface block. The second branch rises upward from a point that lies to the left of the incoming supply line and ends on the left side of the square outline of the contactor. Both branches end on a block or on the contactor outline, and neither branch crosses the incoming supply line, the horizontal run, the sensing line that rises from the circle, or the joining line described above.

The part names listed below are semantic identifiers only and do not appear as drawing text. Each reference numeral sits clear of the line work on a short straight leader that crosses no other leader and no line work.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 108 isolated local bus: leader ends on the bus line left of the dashed rectangle.
- 120 first connector channel: leader ends on the dashed rectangle.
- 122 contactor: leader ends on the square outline straddling the vertical line.
- 124 connector current sensor: leader ends on the circle outline straddling the horizontal run, clear of the sensing line that rises from the circle.
- 126 control-pilot interface: leader ends well inside the lower block within the dashed rectangle.
- 128 vehicle connector: leader ends well inside the block straddling the right side.
- 130 electric vehicle: leader ends well inside the rounded rectangle.

Its upward portion lies to the right of the left side of the vehicle connector block, so that it crosses neither the horizontal run from the contactor nor any other line. Neither end of this joining line is free: one end is on the control-pilot interface block and the other is on the lower edge of the vehicle connector block. No other line extends downward from the vehicle connector block.

Right of the dashed rectangle a larger rounded rectangle represents an electric vehicle, shown schematically. A short solid line joins the right side of the vehicle connector block to the left side of the rounded rectangle.

A solid horizontal line enters from the left edge of the drawing area and crosses the left side of the dashed rectangle in its lower region, as the isolated local bus. Inside the dashed rectangle it branches two ways. One branch continues towards the right side of the drawing area, passing below the corner and below the horizontal run, and ends on the left side of the control-pilot interface block. The second branch rises upward from a point that lies to the left of the incoming supply line and ends on the left side of the square outline of the contactor. Both branches end on a block or on the contactor outline, and neither branch crosses the incoming supply line, the horizontal run, the sensing line that rises from the circle, or the joining line described above.

- 128 vehicle connector: leader ends well inside the block straddling the right side.
